title: Onity Hotel Key Cards Compatibility Guide
summary: A technical compatibility guide for Onity (now Honeywell Onity) hotel lock estates. Covering the HT, ADVANCE, integra and DirectKey mobile generations, chip-family support, Encoder 1100 / 2100 / 4000 workflows, OPERA / Mews / Protel integration and the legacy vulnerabilities properties should remediate before ordering new cards.
heroPoints: Onity lock generations from HT22 through DirectKey span magstripe, MIFARE Classic and DESFire. Identify the generation before specifying chip.
Encoder generation (HT Portable, Encoder 1100, 2100, 4000) constrains which chip family can actually be issued.
Remediate the HT-series firmware remediation before new card orders. Some properties still run exposed firmware lines.

items: Properties refreshing Onity-compatible guest card stock.

Estates with mixed HT-series (magstripe) and ADVANCE / integra (RFID) doors consolidating stock.

brief.label: What to send
items: Onity lock model (HT22, HT24, HT28 Smart, ADVANCE, integra, DirectKey) or a current guest card sample.
Encoder model — HT Portable programmer, Encoder 1100, Encoder 2100 or Encoder 4000 — and PMS name.
Chip-family preference — Classic 1K, Plus or DESFire EV2/EV3 — and whether magstripe is still in issuance.
Artwork needs, pilot quantity and target delivery date.

brief.label: Testing checklist
items: Validate opening on the real lock estate before artwork refinement.
Confirm encoder round-trip — issue, extend, replace, cancel — on a live PMS reservation.
Verify that HT-series locks are on a remediated firmware line before finalising the card order.
Keep one conservative baseline card in the sample plan even if premium materials remain attractive.

sections.title: Onity lock generations and what they accept
sections.intro: Onity — now part of Honeywell — has operated under three hardware eras: the long-running HT magstripe series, the transitional ADVANCE / integra HF RFID generations, and the current DirectKey mobile-plus-card architecture. The generation on the door decides the native credential technology; a single card SKU that covers every Onity estate rarely exists.
paragraphs: Onity was one of the largest magstripe hotel lock vendors globally and many properties still run HT22, HT24 and HT28 Smart locks. Mostly on magstripe, with a subset upgraded to RFID reader modules. Upgrading from HT magstripe to ADVANCE or integra is a door-by-door hardware change, not a firmware flash, which is why mixed estates persist for years.

The 2012 HT-series vulnerability (unauthenticated opening through the DC port) drove a large firmware remediation programme, but not every property participated. Any compatibility discussion that includes HT-series locks should also confirm that the firmware is on the remediated line. New cards do not remediate the vulnerability, but issuing new stock without confirming remediation leaves the property exposed.

callout.label: Firmware remediation reminder
callout.text: If the property still runs HT-series magstripe locks, confirm the board has been on the post-2013 firmware remediation before placing a new card order. New cards do not remediate the vulnerability, but issuing without confirming remediation leaves exposure open.

sections.title: Chip-family compatibility per generation
sections.intro: Onity's HF readers span a Classic-to-DESFire envelope, but each generation has a practical sweet spot. Ordering outside the sweet spot usually works at the lock but introduces PMS or encoder workflow issues.
bullets: MIFARE Classic 1K — the broadest compatibility envelope across Onity RFID generations. Works on ADVANCE, integra and DirectKey; standard for properties that still have any ADVANCE doors in the estate.
MIFARE Plus (SE / S / X). Accepted by integra in SL1 compatibility mode on firmware lines from roughly 2017 onwards; SL3 AES-128 is supported on DirectKey and newer integra firmware.

MIFARE DESFire EV1/EV2/EV3 — native on DirectKey and recent integra firmware; not readable on ADVANCE or earlier. EV3 is recommended over EV1 for new rollouts because of the larger key space and AES-128 originality check.
Magstripe (Track 2) — used by all HT-series locks and some ADVANCE dual-interface retrofits. Onity magstripe is a Track 2 variant with a proprietary data layout.
BLE mobile key (DirectKey). Not a card chip but an app-based credential; coexists with physical cards on the same reservation. Requires a DirectKey-enabled integra or DirectKey generation lock.
125 kHz proximity — not natively supported; Onity hospitality locks have never shipped with a 125 kHz read head.

sections.title: Encoder 1100, 2100, 4000 and the HT Portable programmer
sections.intro: Onity uses four distinct encoder families across its history. The encoder at the front desk — not just the lock at the door — limits which chip families can actually be issued.
bullets: HT Portable programmer — the legacy handheld unit used to program HT-series magstripe locks and issue magstripe cards; not RFID-capable.
Encoder 1100 — the first Onity RFID desktop encoder; supports MIFARE Classic 1K encoding, USB-attached, PC/SC-class. Sufficient for ADVANCE estates but limited for DESFire.
Encoder 2100 — the integra-era desktop encoder; supports Classic, Plus (SL1/SL3) and DESFire EV1/EV2 on current firmware lines. The most common encoder in active Onity estates today.
Encoder 4000 — the DirectKey-era desktop encoder; supports Classic, Plus, DESFire EV2/EV3 and issues BLE mobile keys alongside physical cards. Recommended for new rollouts.
PC/SC conformance — Encoders 2100 and 4000 are PC/SC-class and interoperate with standard Windows smart-card middleware; Encoder 1100 required Onity-specific drivers on older Windows builds.
Encoder firmware is the limiting factor for DESFire on the 2100 — firmware should be verified with Onity service before ordering DESFire stock.

sections.title: PMS integration on the Onity back-end
sections.intro: Onity's PMS integration stack is driven by its HT-Suite back-end (for the HT era) and by the integra / DirectKey certified interfaces in the current generation. The card chip does not depend on the PMS, but the certified interface version determines what gets encoded.
bullets: Oracle OPERA — the most common PMS pairing for Onity; OPERA 5 and OPERA Cloud both certified through the Onity OPERA interface.
Mews — integrated via Mews Connector to integra and DirectKey; supports batch encoding where encoder firmware permits.
Protel — supported on integra through the certified Protel interface; Protel Air (cloud) uses a local Onity encoding agent on the front-desk PC.
Agilysys LMS / rGuest — common in casino and resort estates; certified through the Agilysys Onity interface.
Cloud PMS platforms typically run a local Onity encoding agent (Windows service) on the same workstation as the encoder.
Batch encoding for group arrivals is supported on the Encoder 4000 with DirectKey back-end; older encoders typically encode one card at a time.

sections.title: DirectKey mobile key and physical card coexistence
sections.intro: Onity's mobile-key layer is DirectKey. Unlike a pure-mobile strategy, Onity continues to issue physical cards from the same reservation. Most properties run DirectKey as a guest-choice option rather than a replacement.
bullets: DirectKey issues a BLE key from the DirectKey app server that the guest's phone presents to the lock. The same reservation can also issue a physical card.
The lock must be on DirectKey-certified integra firmware or a DirectKey generation controller; older ADVANCE doors cannot accept DirectKey without a reader-module upgrade.
Mobile-key fallback — DirectKey issues a short-expiry physical card alongside the BLE key by default, so a guest whose phone runs out of battery is not locked out.
BLE range — typically 30–80 cm; deliberately suppressed above 1 m to avoid drive-by false unlocks.
Apple Wallet / Google Wallet. DirectKey supports NFC wallet keys on newer lock firmware; verify with Onity service which firmware line enables wallet emulation on a specific property.

sections.title: Card material and thickness constraints on Onity readers
sections.intro: Onity HF readers are relatively permissive but not unlimited. The constraints below are the ones that most often surface in pilot-to-production transitions.
bullets: Standard ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 thickness (0.76 mm ± 0.08 mm) is the safe default on all Onity generations.
Thicker cards (1.0–1.2 mm) — premium PVC or bamboo — read reliably on integra and DirectKey; ADVANCE readers are tuned narrower and can be marginal above 0.9 mm.
Wood and bamboo cards with DESFire EV3 inlays — acceptable on integra (recent firmware) and DirectKey; pilot a production-thickness sample before committing to a full order.
Anti-metal / metal-edge cards. Not recommended on any Onity generation; the shielding detunes the HF antenna and causes intermittent reads.
Transparent PVC — read-compatible but loses the printed branding surface; used as a secondary or staff card.
Dual-interface (magstripe + RFID) cards. Supported; commonly used in mixed HT-series / ADVANCE estates during migration windows.

sections.title: What to validate before scaling
sections.intro: A disciplined Onity pilot tests both the technical path (chip, reader, encoder firmware) and the operational path (issue, re-encode, cancel, DirectKey if in scope). Scaling before both paths are proven is where most Onity pilots lose time.
bullets: Test the card on at least one door from each generation in scope. ADVANCE, integra and DirectKey readers are not interchangeable from a chip-selection point of view.
Run a full reservation cycle on a live PMS reservation and log encoder, lock-firmware and PMS-driver versions.
If HT-series magstripe is still in the estate, confirm the remediation firmware is deployed before issuing new stock.
Cross-check the DirectKey BLE flow if mobile key is in scope; a card-only pilot will miss wallet-emulation regressions.
Pilot a 100–200 card first production batch before scaling to the full property. Most field failures surface in the first 30 days of live issuance.

faq.question: How do I identify the Onity lock generation before ordering cards?
faq.answer: The HT22, HT24 and HT28 series carry visible HT branding on the escutcheon and are magstripe-only; ADVANCE and integra carry the respective names on the reader plate; DirectKey generation locks typically have a slim NFC/BLE reader module above the handle. If the property is unsure, an Onity service session can report the firmware and hardware model for each connected door. That is the authoritative source.

faq.question: Can one card SKU cover both ADVANCE and DirectKey doors in the same estate?
faq.answer: Yes if the SKU is MIFARE Classic 1K — Classic reads on ADVANCE, integra and DirectKey generations. A DESFire-only SKU will not read on ADVANCE doors and is a mistake on a mixed estate. Most properties consolidate on Classic during migration and switch to DESFire only after the last ADVANCE door is retired.

faq.question: Is the 2012 Onity HT-series vulnerability still relevant for new card orders?
faq.answer: The vulnerability itself is remediated by a firmware update to the HT-series lock board, not by a card change. However, properties that never participated in the remediation programme still run exposed firmware. A compatibility review for an HT estate should confirm remediation status with Onity service before issuing new stock. Issuing new cards does not close the exposure by itself.

faq.question: What encoder do I need for DESFire EV3 on an integra estate?
faq.answer: Encoder 2100 with current firmware supports DESFire EV2/EV3 encoding; Encoder 4000 is the preferred unit for new rollouts. Encoder 1100 cannot issue DESFire and should be upgraded before a DESFire card order is placed.

faq.question: Does DirectKey require the property to run a specific mobile app?
faq.answer: Onity provides a default DirectKey-branded app, but larger hospitality groups typically integrate DirectKey into their own branded app via the Onity mobile SDK. Both options present the same BLE credential to the lock. The integration is a guest-experience choice rather than a technical constraint.

faq.question: Will thicker bamboo or wood cards read reliably on ADVANCE?
faq.answer: Premium-thickness bamboo and wood (1.0–1.2 mm) is tuned for integra and DirectKey readers; ADVANCE readers have a narrower tolerance and can be marginal above 0.9 mm. If the estate has any ADVANCE doors, pilot a production-thickness sample on the real hardware before committing to a full order.

faq.question: What causes the most common encoding failures on Onity?
faq.answer: The top three causes are encoder firmware older than the chip family requires (a 1100 trying to write DESFire), Onity-side PMS driver drift after a PMS upgrade, and sector-key loss after a workstation image refresh. Systematic troubleshooting starts with confirming encoder firmware and testing a known-good card before blaming the new card batch.
